question: It has been proved that the dissolution speed of the solvate that is formed when the griseofulvin and the chloroform are associated, is:

options.opa: Less than the unsolvated form of the drug.
options.opb: Limiting step of the disintegration of the tablets in which the drug is formulated.
options.opc: Greater than the unsolvated form of the drug.
options.opd: Limiting factor of the distribution of the drug to the aqueous sectors of the organism.
options.ope: Same as the unsolvated form of the drug.

analysis: Griseofulvin is known to form solvates, which can influence its dissolution characteristics. Generally, solvated forms can exhibit different dissolution rates compared to their unsolvated counterparts. In this case, the dissolution speed of the solvate formed with chloroform is likely to be greater than that of the unsolvated form, as solvates can enhance solubility and dissolution due to their altered physical properties. Therefore, the correct answer is that the dissolution speed is greater than the unsolvated form of the drug.
